intro: Week 2 is in the books. Two teams are still perfect and two are still looking for their first win.

blurbs.10: Already beat the #2 and #3 teams. The only unbeaten team that has fully earned it.
blurbs.9: Josh Allen's 46.82 was the best individual game of the week. Kelce's 25.1 sat behind Goedert's 1.4, and the 36.1 left on the bench tied for the most in the league.
blurbs.5: Second-best score of the week and a loss to show for it. Nothing wrong here that a little luck won't fix.
blurbs.7: Goff went for 37.78 and it still wasn't enough. Solidly above average, just ran into the Allen show.
blurbs.4: Survived by 0.26 and has faced the fourth-most points in the league. Bryce Young's 30.08 on the bench says the ceiling is higher.
blurbs.8: 2-0 on the eighth-best scoring and the softest schedule in the league, and now officially named 2-0. The team that's 18-0 in all-play is up next.
blurbs.3: From 142.16 in Week 1 to the lowest score of Week 2. Biggest faller.
blurbs.2: 93.44 would have lost to anyone but the team they drew. CeeDee is doing a lot of carrying.
blurbs.6: Winless, but outscoring 1-1 Mayo Clinic and the team named 2-0. Starting DJ Moore (-0.1) didn't help.
blurbs.1: Last in points, and one of the two losses was by 0.26. Same 4-14 all-play record as the team named 2-0, which says plenty about luck.

recap.1: Lamb (31.3) outscored everybody on the field in the lowest-scoring game of the week.
recap.2: Kincaid's 22.5 was just enough. Flip to Best lineups: both teams left 35-plus on the bench, and it still comes down to 0.28 the other way.
recap.3: Allen beat Goff by 9 in the QB duel, and Cook and Henry outscored Tuten and Swift 36.6 to 23.6.
recap.4: Stafford's 34.98 did the heavy lifting against a lineup that got -0.1 out of DJ Moore.
recap.5: Game of the week. JSN and Mahomes edged Purdy, St. Brown and a surprise 26 from Dalton Schultz.

gameday.1: Christian Watson already put up 19.1 on Thursday night, so EZ-Bee-Z starts the day in a hole. Hurts needs a big afternoon, and Jaylen Warren is questionable.
gameday.2: Matthew Golden came off the taxi squad and dropped 18.5 on Thursday. Mayo's path runs through Malik Willis outdueling Josh Allen, which is a lot to ask.
gameday.3: This was a coin flip until Bijan (34.3) and Drake London (23.9) put 58.2 on the board Thursday. Yugi needs McCaffrey, Achane and a questionable Mike Evans to dig out of that.
gameday.4: Butter Boys are running three tight ends again, and Kraft opened with a quiet 6.6. Purdy vs Goff is close on paper, which makes this the most likely upset on the board.
gameday.5: The biggest projected gap of the week at 43.6 points. 2-0 has a lot of pride riding on keeping that name for another week.
